newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber ends week mixed on ringgit, rupiah.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber ends week mixed on ringgit, rupiah.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week mixed after adjusting to the fluctuations of a battered ringgit and rupiah, local traders said on Friday.
Buying of the SMR20 and other selected SMR grades by agents covering earlier sales to foreign clients helped keep prices steady, said traders.

At the close, the benchmark RSS1 for September buyer was officially priced at 250.50 cents (90 cents U.S.), down half cent from Thursday's close. The SMR20 for September buyer was quoted a cent up at 250 cents a kg.
Traders said they expected a similar trend next week.
"We don't know what's happening with the ringgit or rupiah and I don't think our clients know very much either," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.
He added: "Technically, the prices should adjust upwards next week if the ringgit falls again. But then again it might not."
Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Thursday it will no longer announce its daily intervention and conversion bands for the rupiah, causing the currency to plunge against the dollar.
